name: Can accessibility modifications be integrated into a home restoration project?

mainEntity.name: Can accessibility modifications be integrated into a home restoration project?

acceptedAnswer.text: Property restoration provides an ideal opportunity to add accessibility modifications because walls, subfloors, and framing are already open for repair. When restoring bathrooms or entryways, you can widen doorway framing to accommodate mobility devices, add structural blocking between wall studs for secure grab bars, and build zero-barrier roll-in tile showers without paying extra for separate demolition down the road. Addressing accessibility during structural framing and drywall stages saves significant labor costs compared to retrofitting these features into a finished, undamaged room later.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes. Incorporating wider doorways, wall blocking for grab bars, or zero-threshold tile showers while framing and drywall are already exposed saves considerable time and labor.
